tier_reason: Quill README performance section (benchmark code in odygrd/logger_benchmarks, GCC 14.2, Release with -march=x86-64-v3, Intel Core i5-12600) shows fmtlog 6 ns vs spdlog 271 ns p50 on 1-thread numbers; fmtlog's own bench/bench.cc table on Xeon Gold 6144 matches the record's numbers but states no flags.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README (bench/bench.cc, Xeon Gold 6144, spdlog basic_logger_st): staticString 6.4 ns vs spdlog 156.4 ns; stringConcat 6.4 vs 209.4; singleInteger 6.3 vs 202.3; twoIntegers 6.4 vs 257.2; singleDouble 6.2 vs 225.0; complexFormat 6.4 vs 390.9 ns. Quill README (int,int,double, 1 thread): fmtlog 6 ns vs spdlog 271 ns at p50; 4 threads 8 vs 557 ns; std::vector<std::string> 1 thread 774 vs 6906 ns. Backend throughput in quill's table is near parity: fmtlog 2.69M msg/s vs spdlog 2.57M msg/s.
corrections.caveats: Own README table at https://github.com/MengRao/fmtlog (compiler flags not stated there; spdlog run as synchronous basic_logger_st, so its latency includes formatting and I/O). Tier A relies on quill's harness (odygrd/logger_benchmarks, quill is a competing logger). The gain is caller-thread latency only: backend throughput to file is roughly equal to spdlog (2.69 vs 2.57M msg/s in quill's table).

notes: Numbers confirmed on both pages. Last commit 2025-02-13 (stale), MIT, 1.0k stars, not archived.
